analysis.title: Global Equity Strategy: 2027 Outlook: Finding Value in Growth
key_insights: GS expects global equities to keep rising in 2027 with higher volatility. Valuations have de-rated, nominal growth and earnings growth stay positive but slower, and bond yields, inflation and oil prices are expected to fall.

Focus is Growth balanced with selective Defensives and beneficiaries of lower bond yields and oil prices. Long-duration Growth, particularly US Hyperscalers, is the preferred entry point as growth rates slow.

Regional stance on a risk-adjusted basis: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia ex Japan and EM, underweight Europe. Forecast returns are highest in Asia, but concentration and volatility cap the risk-adjusted case.
2026 had three features: returns were similar across regions (reversing the 2009-2025 US dominance), earnings growth was the main return driver, and all markets de-rated.
Earnings growth is expected to at least halve in nearly all markets in 2027: US 36% to 11%, Europe about 18% to 7%, Japan 24% to 9%, Asia from close to 80% to under 30%.

Drivers of the slowdown: hyperscaler capex growth slows (its EPS contribution goes from +12pp in 2026 to -5pp in 2028), depreciation and interest costs rise, and energy prices moderate. Consensus has IT EPS growth falling from about 90% to 45%, Communication Services from 34% to -5%, Energy from 99% to about -10%, Materials from 45% to 12%.

Cost of capital remains higher. Rates strategists expect a modest tightening cycle and slow progress toward cuts in 2027. Bond strategists see some relief in long-term yields, but credit strategists expect spreads to widen.

Valuations: the US P/E has fallen from near its 100th percentile over 20 years to 18.5x. Global P/E is around its 35-year average. Global Tech is in the 20th percentile of its 20-year range and IT is one of the cheapest sectors. Hyperscalers trade at 19.7x, below the previous 20-year range and below Consumer Staples.

Hyperscalers have nearly closed the valuation gap with the other 495 S&P 500 stocks. Biggest companies have turned cash flow negative but net debt/equity remains healthy, so GS treats them as relatively defensive.

The Value factor is near the 90th percentile of its 20-year range and is more expensive than Growth relative to history. The Value vs Growth valuation gap has narrowed after Value outperformed sharply in all regions in recent months.

Selective cyclical growth: Korean memory is priced for a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings despite sold-out DRAM and HBM through 2029, and trades at 0.7x 2028 P/B, which has historically signaled strong forward returns. Volatility stays high.

Selective Defensives rather than a broad defensive shift. Focus on US Healthcare, Power and Buyback Aristocrats, Asian shareholder-return and secure-dividend names, and European Telecoms and Utilities.

Lower oil and yields: Brent is forecast to fall from about $100/bbl at end-2026 to $78/bbl at end-2027, turning a 0.4pp growth drag into a modest boost. The Fed and ECB should move toward cuts in late 2027, and GS rates forecasts are more dovish than market pricing. Europe is the clearest beneficiary.
EM index concentration is at a record: Korea and Taiwan are about half of MSCI EM, Info Tech is over 40%, and TSMC, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are about 30%.

Four risks, each two-sided: bond volatility, oil volatility, weaker AI capex, and momentum and concentration. US large-cap tech is seen as more defensive than Asian tech, so concentration risk is higher in Asia.

sector_views.rationale: Valuations have fallen sharply, balance sheets are strong, and earnings growth is slower but still strong. They should benefit from lower yields.
Sharp de-rating leaves upside convexity, but outcomes depend heavily on AI capex and volatility will stay high.
A selective Defensive that has re-rated and whose growth is not slowing, favored in the US, Asia and EM.
Oil is forecast lower, and consensus has Energy EPS growth turning from 99% in 2026 to about -10% in 2027.
Defensive sectors that also benefit from lower bond yields.
Cyclicals have already de-rated, but lower yields would hamper relative performance of Cyclicals and Financials.

earnings_insights: GS top-down 2027 EPS growth: S&P 500 11% (from 36% in 2026), STOXX 600 7% (from about 18%), TOPIX 9% (from 24%), MSCI AP ex Japan 26%, MSCI EM 26%. All are GS estimates.

Consensus 2027E EPS growth: S&P 500 16.5%, STOXX 600 8.4%, TOPIX 13.2%, MSCI AC World 17.0%, IT 45.3%, Communication Services -5.2%, Energy -11.3%, Health Care 17.7%. 2026E consensus EPS growth: S&P 500 32.4%, IT 89.2%, Energy 99.1%.
Consensus net margins for 2027E: S&P 500 17.1% (16.2% in 2026E), IT 31.6%, Financials 22.9%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower energy prices turn a 0.4pp drag on global growth into a modest boost, lower inflation, and favor Europe and consumers while pressuring Energy earnings.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Lower oil would reduce inflation and rate expectations, boosting long-duration Growth and defensive growth valuations.

macro_indicators.reading: Rate cuts expected in late 2027, after a modest tightening cycle and slow progress toward cuts
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS rates forecasts are more dovish than market pricing, supporting modestly lower bond yields.

macro_indicators.reading: Slowing in 2027 as the AI investment boom peaks
macro_indicators.interpretation: Equities typically rise while nominal GDP is growing, but slower growth makes growth scarcer and rewarded.

macro_indicators.reading: Long-term yields remain elevated, with some relief forecast
macro_indicators.interpretation: Relief in long-term yields would support equities and favor defensive and long-duration areas over Cyclicals and Financials.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US Hyperscalers as long-duration Growth with strong balance sheets
trade_ideas.rationale: P/E has fallen to 19.7x, the premium to the other 495 S&P stocks has nearly closed, and earnings growth stays strong though slower.
trade_ideas.risk: Weaker AI capex and momentum concentration.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight selective cyclical growth in Korean memory and chips
trade_ideas.rationale: Korean memory prices in a 70% cut to 2027 consensus earnings despite products sold out until 2029, and trades at 0.7x 2028 P/B.
trade_ideas.risk: Highly dependent on AI capex pace, with high volatility and a wide range of outcomes.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia ex Japan and EM, underweight Europe
trade_ideas.rationale: Reflects relative growth, profitability, valuation and risk-adjusted returns.
trade_ideas.risk: Bond yield spikes, oil volatility, AI capex shift.

trade_ideas.description: Selective Defensives: US Healthcare, Power and Buyback Aristocrats; European Telecoms and Utilities
trade_ideas.rationale: Offers reasonable valuations and benefits from potentially lower bond yields as growth slows.
trade_ideas.risk: Many traditional Defensives no longer look cheap.

risk_factors: Bond volatility: sovereign debt concerns could spike yields, especially in Europe, while easing inflation could produce a rally.
Oil price volatility, with risks in both directions around the $88 Brent forecast for 2027.
Weaker AI capex, which could de-rate memory, chips and Industrials that benefit from the capex boom.
Narrow breadth and concentration in the US and Asia, which raise the risk of momentum reversals.
Credit spreads could widen as growth slows.
Lower oil would cut Energy earnings growth, weighing more on Europe.
charts_described: Exhibit 5: GS top-down EPS growth 2026 vs 2027 is 36% to 11% for the S&P 500, 18% to 7% for the STOXX 600, 24% to 9% for TOPIX.
Exhibit 6: Estimated contribution of Hyperscaler capex to S&P 500 EPS growth is 2pp in 2024, 5pp in 2025, 12pp in 2026, 9pp in 2027 and -5pp in 2028.
vol_and_positioning: GS expects equities to rise in 2027 with higher volatility than in recent years, and says the range of outcomes has widened.
MXAPJ YTD annualised volatility is 24.2%, the basis for a neutral volatility-adjusted stance on Asia ex Japan and EM.
Concentration is high: EM top 3 stocks are about 30% of MSCI EM and Korea plus Taiwan about half. Narrow breadth raises stock volatility and momentum factor risk.
Value has sharply outperformed Growth in all regions in recent months, and the Cyclicals vs Defensives P/E premium has compressed sharply.
geopolitical: Some normalisation in the Middle East and a recovery in Persian Gulf supply should reduce geopolitical risk premia and lower commodity prices, including European gas prices.
Fading US tariff effects are cited as a factor lowering inflation in 2027.
Europe faces a heavy political calendar and government debt issues, with sovereign debt risks highest in an election-heavy year.

tension_points.theme: AI capex peak versus Hyperscaler value
tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers have de-rated to 19.7x P/E, have strong balance sheets and diversified income, and continue to enjoy strong but slower earnings growth. Lower yields favor long-duration Growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler capex growth slows, which cuts the EPS contribution from +12pp in 2026 to -5pp in 2028. Depreciation and interest costs rise, and the largest companies have turned cash flow negative.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharper-than-expected slowdown in AI capex, which GS says could de-rate memory, chips and capex-beneficiary Industrials.

tension_points.bull_case: Brent falls to $78/bbl by end-2027 and yields ease, lowering inflation and supporting long-duration Growth, consumers and European equities.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil and yields could spike, and sovereign debt concerns could push yields higher, especially in Europe.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further spike in bond yields on sovereign debt concerns, or oil rising rather than falling in 2027.

theme_stances.key_argument: Hyperscalers have de-rated and have strong balance sheets, making them attractive long-duration Growth as growth rates slow.
Earnings growth is on course to at least halve across major regions as AI capex growth peaks and costs rise.
theme_stances.evidence: Earnings growth poised to more than halve across major markets in 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: Lower oil helps the European economy but weighs on earnings growth, valuations have not fallen as much, and government debt and the political calendar add risk.
